#### problem.saveAs

_**Purpose:**_

   Saves the current data structures, i.e. matrices, control settings and problem attribute settings to file and terminates the run so that optimization can be resumed later.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
File IO, Save Restore, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.saveAs(filename="")`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`filename: str` | The name of the file \(without .svf\) to save to. 

_**Further information:**_
1. The data structures are written to the file _problem_name_ `.svf`. Optimization may recommence from the same point when the data structures are restored by a call to `problem.restore`. Note that the `.svf` files created are particular to the release of the Optimizer used to create them. They can only be read using the same release Optimizer as used to create them.
2. The function `problem.saveAs` is equivalent to `problem.save` with the exception of allowing to adjust the name of the file created. The name of the file must not be greater than `MAXPROBNAMELENGTH`.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.restore`.

#### problem.restore

_**Purpose:**_

   Restores the Optimizer's data structures from a file created by`problem.saveAs`. Optimization may then recommence from the point at which the file was created.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
File IO, Save Restore, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.restore(probname="", flags="")`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`probname: str` | | A string of up to `MAXPROBNAMELENGTH` characters containing the problem name. 
`flags: str` |  | Additional flags
&nbsp; | `h` | Do not restore hardware information from the file;
&nbsp; | `v` | use the provided filename verbatim, without appending the `.svf` extension.

_**Further information:**_
This routine restores the data structures from the file _problem_name_ `.svf`that was created by a previous execution of `problem.saveAs`. Note that `.svf`files are particular to the release of the Optimizer used to create them. They can only be read using the same major release of the Optimizer that was used to create them.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.saveAs`.

#### problem.pivot

_**Purpose:**_

   Performs a simplex pivot by bringing variable `enter`into the basis and removing `leave`.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Linear Algebra, Simplex, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.pivot(enter, leave)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`enter: var | constraint` | Index of row or column to enter basis. 
`leave: var | constraint` | Index of row or column to leave basis. 

_**Error values:**_

Code | Description 
---------- | ----------
425 | `enter`is invalid \(out of range or already basic\).
426 | `leave`is invalid \(out of range or not eligible, e.g. nonbasic, zero pivot, etc.\).

_**Related controls:**_

_Double_
  
_Name_ | _Description_
---------- | ----------
`PIVOTTOL` | Pivot tolerance.
`RELPIVOTTOL` | Relative pivot tolerance.

_**Further information:**_
1. Row indices are in the range `0` to `ROWS` - `1`, whilst columns are in the range `ROWS` + `SPAREROWS` to `ROWS` + `SPAREROWS` + `COLS` - `1`.
2. Arguments ``enter`,  `leave`` may contain either`xpress.var` or`xpress.constraint` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getPivotOrder`, `problem.getPivots`.

#### problem.loadLPSol

_**Purpose:**_

   Loads an LP solution for the problem into the Optimizer.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Solution, LP, Data Input, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `status = problem.loadLPSol(x=None, slack=None, duals=None, djs=None)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`x: Iterable[float]` | Optional: Double array of length `COLS` \(for the original problem and not the presolve problem\) containing the values of the variables. May be `None`, see further information. 
`slack: Iterable[float]` | Optional: double array of length `ROWS` containing the values of slack variables. May be `None`, see further information. 
`duals: Iterable[float]` | Optional: double array of length `ROWS` containing the values of dual variables. May be `None`, see further information. 
`djs: Iterable[float]` | Optional: double array of length `COLS` containing the values of reduced costs. May be `None`, see further information. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`status: int` | The status. The status is one of:
&nbsp; | `0` | Solution is loaded.
&nbsp; | `1` | Solution is not loaded because the problem is in presolved status.

_**Further information:**_
1. If neither variable values nor dual values are provided, the current solution in memory will be unloaded.
2. When variables `x` is `None`, the variables will be set to their bounds.
3. When slack variables `slack` is `None`, it will be computed from variables `x`. If slacks are provided, variables cannot be omitted.
4. When dual variables `duals` is `None`, both dual variables and reduced costs will be set to zero.
5. When reduced costs `djs` is `None`, it will be computed from dual variables `duals`. If reduced costs are provided, dual variables cannot be omitted.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getSolution`, `problem.crossoverLpSol`.

#### problem.repairWeightedInfeas

_**Purpose:**_

   By relaxing a set of selected constraints and bounds of an infeasible problem, it attempts to identify a 'solution' that violates the selected set of constraints and bounds minimally, while satisfying all other constraints and bounds. Among such solution candidates, it selects one that is optimal regarding the original objective function.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Infeasibility, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `status = problem.repairWeightedInfeas(lepref, gepref, lbpref, ubpref, phase2, delta, flags)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`lepref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `ROWS` containing the preferences for relaxing the less or equal side of row. 
`gepref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `ROWS` containing the preferences for relaxing the greater or equal side of a row. 
`lbpref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `COLS` containing the preferences for relaxing lower bounds. 
`ubpref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `COLS` containing preferences for relaxing upper bounds. 
`phase2: str` |  | Controls the second phase of optimization:
&nbsp; | `o` | use the objective sense of the original problem \(default\);
&nbsp; | `x` | maximize the relaxed problem using the original objective;
&nbsp; | `f` | skip optimization regarding the original objective;
&nbsp; | `n` | minimize the relaxed problem using the original objective;
&nbsp; | `i` | if the relaxation is infeasible, generate an irreducible infeasible subset for the analysis of the problem;
&nbsp; | `a` | if the relaxation is infeasible, generate all irreducible infeasible subsets for the analysis of the problem.
`delta: float` | | The relaxation multiplier in the second phase -1. 
`flags: str` | | Specifies flags to be passed to problem.optimize. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`status: int` | The status after the relaxation:
&nbsp; | `0` | relaxed optimum found;
&nbsp; | `1` | relaxed problem is infeasible;
&nbsp; | `2` | relaxed problem is unbounded;
&nbsp; | `3` | solution of the relaxed problem regarding the original objective is nonoptimal;
&nbsp; | `4` | error \(when return code is nonzero\);
&nbsp; | `5` | numerical instability;
&nbsp; | `6` | analysis of an infeasible relaxation was performed, but the relaxation is feasible.

_**Further information:**_
1. This function applies to all problem types.
2. A row or bound is relaxed by introducing a new nonnegative variable that will contain the infeasibility of the row or bound. Suppose for example that row a<sup>T</sup> x = b is relaxed from below. Then a new variable \('infeasibility breaker'\) _s≥0_  is added to the row, which becomes a<sup>T</sup> x + s = b. Observe that a<sup>T</sup> x may now take smaller values than b. To minimize such violations, the weighted sum of these new variables is minimized.
3. A preference of 0 results in the row or bound not being relaxed. The higher the preference, the more willing the modeller is to relax a given row or bound.
4. The weight of each infeasibility breaker in the objective minimizing the violations is 1/p, where `p` is the preference associated with the infeasibility breaker. Thus the higher the preference is, the lower a penalty is associated with the infeasibility breaker while minimizing the violations.
5. If a feasible solution is identified for the relaxed problem, with a sum of violations `p`, then the sum of violations is restricted to be no greater than \( `1+delta`\) `p`, and the problem is optimized with respect to the original objective function. A nonzero delta increases the freedom of the original problem. The weighted sum of violations will be available in `PENALTYVALUE`.
6. Note that on some problems, slight modifications of delta may affect the value of the original objective drastically.
7. The default value for delta in the console is 0.001.
8. Note that because of their special associated modeling properties, binary and semi-continuous variables are not relaxed.
9. If `pflags` is set such that each penalty is the reciprocal of the preference, the following rules are applied while introducing the auxiliary variables:



__Pref. array__ | __Affects__ | __Relaxation__ | __Cost if pref. `>`0__ | __Cost if pref. `<`0__ | 
---------- |  ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | 
`lepref` | `= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x - aux_var = b` | `1/lrp*aux_var` | `1/lrp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`lepref` | `<= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x - aux_var <= b` | `1/lrp*aux_var` | `1/lrp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`gepref` | `= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x + aux_var = b` | `1/grp*aux_var` | `1/grp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`gepref` | `>= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x + aux_var >= b` | `1/grp*aux_var` | `1/grp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`ubpref` | `upper bounds` | `x<sub>i</sub> - aux_var <= u` | `1/ubp*aux_var` | `1/ubp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`lbpref` | `lower bounds` | `x<sub>i</sub> + aux_var >= l` | `1/lbp*aux_var` | `1/lbp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 

10. If an irreducible infeasible set \(IIS\) has been identified, the generated IIS\(s\) are accessible through the IIS retrieval functions, see `NUMIIS` and `problem.getIISData`.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.repairInfeas`, `problem.repairWeightedInfeasBounds`, `problem.optimize`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.repairWeightedInfeasBounds

_**Purpose:**_

   An extended version of`problem.repairWeightedInfeas`that allows for bounding the level of relaxation allowed.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Infeasibility, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `status = problem.repairWeightedInfeasBounds(lepref, gepref, lbpref, ubpref, lerelax, gerelax, lbrelax, ubrelax, phase2, delta, flags)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`lepref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `ROWS` containing the preferences for relaxing the less or equal side of row. For the console use `-lrp` value. 
`gepref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `ROWS` containing the preferences for relaxing the greater or equal side of a row. For the console use `-grp` value. 
`lbpref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `COLS` containing the preferences for relaxing lower bounds. For the console use `-lbp` value. 
`ubpref: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `COLS` containing preferences for relaxing upper bounds. For the console use `-ubp` value. 
`lerelax: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `ROWS` containing the upper bounds on the amount the less or equal side of a row can be relaxed. For the console use `-lrb` value. 
`gerelax: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `ROWS` containing the upper bounds on the amount the greater or equal side of a row can be relaxed. For the console use `-grb` value. 
`lbrelax: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `COLS` containing the upper bounds on the amount the lower bounds can be relaxed. For the console use `-lbb` value. 
`ubrelax: Iterable[float]` | | Array of size `COLS` containing the upper bounds on the amount the upper bounds can be relaxed. For the console use `-ubb` value. 
`phase2: str` |  | Controls the second phase of optimization:
&nbsp; | `o` | use the objective sense of the original problem \(default\);
&nbsp; | `x` | maximize the relaxed problem using the original objective;
&nbsp; | `f` | skip optimization regarding the original objective;
&nbsp; | `n` | minimize the relaxed problem using the original objective;
&nbsp; | `i` | if the relaxation is infeasible, generate an irreducible infeasible subset for the analysis of the problem;
&nbsp; | `a` | if the relaxation is infeasible, generate all irreducible infeasible subsets for the analysis of the problem.
`delta: float` | | The relaxation multiplier in the second phase -1. 
`flags: str` | | Specifies flags to be passed to problem.optimize. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`status: int` | The status after the relaxation:
&nbsp; | `0` | relaxed optimum found;
&nbsp; | `1` | relaxed problem is infeasible;
&nbsp; | `2` | relaxed problem is unbounded;
&nbsp; | `3` | solution of the relaxed problem regarding the original objective is nonoptimal;
&nbsp; | `4` | error \(when return code is nonzero\);
&nbsp; | `5` | numerical instability;
&nbsp; | `6` | analysis of an infeasible relaxation was performed, but the relaxation is feasible.

_**Further information:**_
1. This function applies to all problem types.
2. A row or bound is relaxed by introducing a new nonnegative variable that will contain the infeasibility of the row or bound. Suppose for example that row a<sup>T</sup> x = b is relaxed from below. Then a new variable \('infeasibility breaker'\) _s≥0_  is added to the row, which becomes a<sup>T</sup> x + s = b. Observe that a<sup>T</sup> x may now take smaller values than b. To minimize such violations, the weighted sum of these new variables is minimized.
3. A preference of 0 results in the row or bound not being relaxed. The higher the preference, the more willing the modeller is to relax a given row or bound.
4. A negative preference indicates that a quadratic penalty cost should be applied. This can specified on a per constraint side or bound basis.
5. If a feasible solution is identified for the relaxed problem, with a sum of violations `p`, then the sum of violations is restricted to be no greater than \( `1+delta`\) `p`, and the problem is optimized with respect to the original objective function. A nonzero delta increases the freedom of the original problem. The weighted sum of violations will be available in `PENALTYVALUE`.
6. Note that on some problems, slight modifications of delta may affect the value of the original objective drastically.
7. The default value for delta in the console is 0.001.
8. Note that because of their special associated modeling properties, binary and semi-continuous variables are not relaxed.
9. Given any row `j` with preferences `lrp=lepref[j]` and `grp=gepref[j]`, or variable `i` with bound preferences `ubp=ubpref[i]` and `lbp=lbpref[i]`, the following rules are applied while introducing the auxiliary variables:



__Preference__ | __Affects__ | __Relaxation__ | __Cost if pref. `>`0__ | __Cost if pref. `<`0__ | 
---------- |  ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | 
`lrp` | `= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x - aux_var = b` | `1/lrp*aux_var` | `1/lrp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`lrp` | `<= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x - aux_var <= b` | `1/lrp*aux_var` | `1/lrp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`grp` | `= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x + aux_var = b` | `1/grp*aux_var` | `1/grp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`grp` | `>= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x + aux_var >= b` | `1/grp*aux_var` | `1/grp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`ubp` | `upper bounds` | `x<sub>i</sub> - aux_var <= u` | `1/ubp*aux_var` | `1/ubp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`lbp` | `lower bounds` | `x<sub>i</sub> + aux_var >= l` | `1/lbp*aux_var` | `1/lbp*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 

10. Only positive bounds are applied; a zero or negative bound is ignored and the amount of relaxation allowed for the corresponding row or bound is not limited. The effect of a zero bound on a row or bound would be equivalent with not relaxing it, and can be achieved by setting its preference array value to zero instead, or not including it in the preference arrays.
11. If an irreducible infeasible set \(IIS\) has been identified, the generated IIS\(s\) are accessible through the IIS retrieval functions, see `NUMIIS` and `problem.getIISData`.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.repairInfeas`, `problem.optimize`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.repairInfeas

_**Purpose:**_

   Provides a simplified interface for`problem.repairWeightedInfeas`.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Infeasibility, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `status = problem.repairInfeas(penalty, phase2, flags, lepref, gepref, lbpref, ubpref, delta)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`penalty: str` |  | The type of penalties created from the preferences:
&nbsp; | `c` | each penalty is the reciprocal of the preference \(default\);
&nbsp; | `s` | the penalties are placed in the scaled problem.
`phase2: str` |  | Controls the second phase of optimization:
&nbsp; | `o` | use the objective sense of the original problem \(default\);
&nbsp; | `x` | maximize the relaxed problem using the original objective;
&nbsp; | `f` | skip optimization regarding the original objective;
&nbsp; | `n` | minimize the relaxed problem using the original objective;
&nbsp; | `i` | if the relaxation is infeasible, generate an irreducible infeasible subset for the analysis of the problem;
&nbsp; | `a` | if the relaxation is infeasible, generate all irreducible infeasible subsets for the analysis of the problem.
`flags: str` | | Specifies flags to be passed to problem.optimize. 
`lepref: float` | | Preference for relaxing the less or equal side of row. 
`gepref: float` | | Preference for relaxing the greater or equal side of a row. 
`lbpref: float` | | Preferences for relaxing lower bounds. 
`ubpref: float` | | Preferences for relaxing upper bounds. 
`delta: float` | | The relaxation multiplier in the second phase -1. For console use `-d` value. A positive value means a relative relaxation by multiplying the first phase objective with \( `delta-1`\), while a negative value means an absolute relaxation, by adding `abs(delta)` to the first phase objective. 

_**Related controls:**_

_Integer_
  
_Name_ | _Description_
---------- | ----------
`DEFAULTALG` | Forced algorithm selection \(default for repairinfeas is primal\).

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`status: int` | The status after the relaxation:
&nbsp; | `0` | relaxed optimum found;
&nbsp; | `1` | relaxed problem is infeasible;
&nbsp; | `2` | relaxed problem is unbounded;
&nbsp; | `3` | solution of the relaxed problem regarding the original objective is nonoptimal;
&nbsp; | `4` | error \(when return code is nonzero\);
&nbsp; | `5` | numerical instability;
&nbsp; | `6` | analysis of an infeasible relaxation was performed, but the relaxation is feasible.

_**Further information:**_
1. This function applies to all problem types.
2. A row or bound is relaxed by introducing a new nonnegative variable that will contain the infeasibility of the row or bound. Suppose for example that row a<sup>T</sup> x = b is relaxed from below. Then a new variable \(infeasibility breaker\) _s≥0_  is added to the row, which becomes a<sup>T</sup> x + s = b. Observe that a<sup>T</sup> x may now take smaller values than b. To minimize such violations, the weighted sum of these new variables is minimized.
3. A preference of 0 results in the row or bound not being relaxed.
4. A negative preference indicates that a quadratic penalty cost should be applied. This can specified on a per constraint side or bound basis.
5. Note that the set of preferences are scaling independent.
6. If a feasible solution is identified for the relaxed problem, with a sum of violations p, then the sum of violations is restricted to be no greater than \( `1+delta`\) `p`, and the problem is optimized with respect to the original objective function. A nonzero delta increases the freedom of the original problem. The weighted sum of violations will be available in `PENALTYVALUE`.
7. Note that on some problems, slight modifications of delta may affect the value of the original objective drastically.
8. The default value for delta in the console is 0.001.
9. Note that because of their special associated modeling properties, binary and semi-continuous variables are not relaxed.
10. The default algorithm for the first phase is the simplex algorithm, since the primal problem can be efficiently warm started in case of the extended problem. These may be altered by setting the value of control `DEFAULTALG`.
11. If `penalty` is set such that each penalty is the reciprocal of the preference, the following rules are applied while introducing the auxiliary variables:



__Preference__ | __Affects__ | __Relaxation__ | __Cost if pref. `>`0__ | __Cost if pref. `<`0__ | 
---------- |  ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | 
`lepref` | `= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x - aux_var = b` | `1/lepref*aux_var` | `1/lepref*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`lepref` | `<= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x - aux_var <= b` | `1/lepref*aux_var` | `1/lepref*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`gepref` | `= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x + aux_var = b` | `1/gepref*aux_var` | `1/gepref*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`gepref` | `>= rows` | `a<sup>T</sup> x + aux_var >= b` | `1/gepref*aux_var` | `1/gepref*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`ubpref` | `upper bounds` | `x<sub>i</sub> - aux_var <= u` | `1/ubpref*aux_var` | `1/ubpref*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 
`lbpref` | `lower bounds` | `x<sub>i</sub> + aux_var >= l` | `1/lbpref*aux_var` | `1/lbpref*aux_var<sup>2</sup>` | 

12. If an irreducible infeasible set \(IIS\) has been identified, the generated IIS\(s\) are accessible through the IIS retrieval functions, see `NUMIIS` and `problem.getIISData`.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.repairWeightedInfeas`, `problem.optimize`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.basisStability

_**Purpose:**_

   Calculates various measures for the stability of the current basis, including the basis condition number.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Linear Algebra, LP, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `value = problem.basisStability(type, norm, scaled)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`type: int` |  | 
&nbsp; | `0` | Condition number of the basis.
&nbsp; | `1` | Stability measure for the solution relative to the current basis.
&nbsp; | `2` | Stability measure for the duals relative to the current basis.
&nbsp; | `3` | Stability measure for the right hand side relative to the current basis.
&nbsp; | `4` | Stability measure for the basic part of the objective relative to the current basis.
`norm: int` |  | 
&nbsp; | `0` | Use the infinity norm.
&nbsp; | `1` | Use the 1 norm.
&nbsp; | `2` | Use the Euclidian norm for vectors, and the Frobenius norm for matrices.
`scaled: int` | | If the stability values are to be calculated in the scaled, or the unscaled matrix. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`value: float` | The calculated value. 

_**Further information:**_
1. The condition number \( `type` = `0`\) of an invertible matrix is the norm of the matrix multiplied with the norm of its inverse. This number is an indication of how accurate the solution can be calculated and how sensitive it is to small changes in the data. The larger the condition number is, the less accurate the solution is likely to become.
2. The stability measures \( `type` = `1...4`\) are using the original matrix and the basis to recalculate the various vectors related to the solution and the duals. The returned stability measure is the norm of the difference of the recalculated vector to the original one.

#### problem.objSA

_**Purpose:**_

   Returns upper and lower sensitivity ranges for specified objective function coefficients. If the objective coefficients are varied within these ranges the current basis remains optimal and the reduced costs remain valid.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Sensitivity Analysis, LP, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `lower, upper = problem.objSA(colind)`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`colind: Iterable[var]` | Integer array containing the indices of the columns whose objective function coefficients sensitivity ranges are required. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`lower: list[float]` | Double array containing the objective function lower range values. 
`upper: list[float]` | Double array containing the objective function upper range values. 

_**Further information:**_
1. This function does not currently apply to general nonlinear problems.
2. `problem.objSA` can only be called when an optimal solution to the current LP has been found. It cannot be used when the problem is MIP presolved.
3. Argument ``colind`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.rhsSA`, `problem.bndSA`.

#### problem.bndSA

_**Purpose:**_

   Returns upper and lower sensitivity ranges for specified variables' lower and upper bounds. If the bounds are varied within these ranges the current basis remains optimal and feasible.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Sensitivity Analysis, LP, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `lblower, lbupper, ublower, ubupper = problem.bndSA(colind)`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`colind: Iterable[var]` | Integer array containing the indices of the columns whose bounds' ranges are required. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`lblower: list[float]` | Double array containing the variable lower bound lower range values. 
`lbupper: list[float]` | Double array containing the variable lower bound upper range values. 
`ublower: list[float]` | Double array containing the variable upper bound lower range values. 
`ubupper: list[float]` | Double array containing the variable upper bound upper range values. 

_**Further information:**_
1. `problem.bndSA` can only be called when an optimal solution to the current LP has been found. It cannot be used when the problem is MIP presolved.
2. Argument ``colind`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.rhsSA`, `problem.objSA`.

#### problem.rhsSA

_**Topic areas:**_

_**Synopsis:**_

   `lower, upper = problem.rhsSA(rowind)`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description

`upper: list[float]` | Double array containing the RHS upper range values. 

_**Further information:**_
1. This function currently does not apply to general nonlinear problems.
2. `problem.rhsSA` can only be called when an optimal solution to the current LP has been found. It cannot be used when the problem is MIP presolved.
3. Argument ``rowind`` may contain either`xpress.constraint` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.objSA`, `problem.bndSA`.

#### problem.addQMatrix

_**Purpose:**_

   Adds a new quadratic matrix into a row defined by triplets.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Creation, Quadratic, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.addQMatrix(row, rowqcol1, rowqcol2, rowqcoef)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`row: constraint` | Index of the row where the quadratic matrix is to be added. 
`rowqcol1: Iterable[var]` | First index in the triplets. 
`rowqcol2: Iterable[var]` | Second index in the triplets. 
`rowqcoef: Iterable[float]` | Coefficients in the triplets. 

_**Further information:**_
1. The triplets should be filled to define the upper-triangular part of the quadratic expression. This means that to add `[x<sup>2</sup>  + 6 xy]` the `rowqcoef` array shall contain the coefficients 1 and 3, respectively.
2. This function cannot be called while the current problem is being solved or when it is in an interrupted state. Use `problem.postSolve` to restore the problem to a non-solving state.
3. Argument ``row`` may contain either`xpress.constraint` objects or integer indices.
4. Arguments ``rowqcol1`,  `rowqcol2`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.loadQCQP`, `problem.getQRowCoeff`, `problem.chgQRowCoeff`, `problem.getQRowQMatrix`, `problem.getQRowQMatrixTriplets`, `problem.getQRows`, `problem.chgQObj`, `problem.chgMQObj`, `problem.getQObj`.

#### problem.delQMatrix

_**Purpose:**_

   Deletes the quadratic part of a row or of the objective function.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Creation, Quadratic, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.delQMatrix(row)`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`row: constraint` | Index of row from which the quadratic part is to be deleted. 

_**Further information:**_
1. If a row index of `-1` is used, the function deletes the quadratic coefficients from the objective function.
2. This function cannot be called while the current problem is being solved or when it is in an interrupted state. Use `problem.postSolve` to restore the problem to a non-solving state.
3. Argument ``row`` may contain either`xpress.constraint` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.addRows`, `problem.delCols`, `problem.delRows`.

#### problem.loadQCQP

_**Purpose:**_

   Used to load a quadratic problem with quadratic side constraints into the Optimizer data structure. Such a problem may have quadratic terms in its objective function as well as in its constraints.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Input, Quadratic, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.loadQCQP(probname="", rowtype=None, rhs=None, rng=None, objcoef=None, start=None, collen=None, rowind=None, rowcoef=None, lb=None, ub=None, objqcol1=None, objqcol2=None, objqcoef=None, qrowind=None, nrowqcoefs=None, rowqcol1=None, rowqcol2=None, rowqcoef=None)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`probname: str` | | A string of up to `MAXPROBNAMELENGTH` characters containing a name for the problem. If `probname` is `None`, the problem name will be an empty string. 
`rowtype: Iterable[str]` |  | Character array containing the row types:
&nbsp; | `L` | indicates a `<=` constraint \(use this one for quadratic constraints as well\);
&nbsp; | `E` | indicates an `=` constraint;
&nbsp; | `G` | indicates a `>=` constraint;
&nbsp; | `R` | indicates a range constraint;
&nbsp; | `N` | indicates a nonbinding constraint.
&nbsp; |  | May be `None`if the problem contains no rows.
`rhs: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the right hand side coefficients of the rows. The right hand side value for a range row gives the upper bound on the row. May be `None` if the problem contains no rows. 
`rng: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the range values for range rows. Values for all other rows will be ignored. May be `None` if there are no ranged constraints. The lower bound on a range row is the right hand side value minus the range value. The sign of the range value is ignored - the absolute value is used in all cases. 
`objcoef: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the objective function coefficients. This can be `None` to set all objective coefficients to 0 \(zero\). 
`start: Iterable[int]` | | Integer array containing the offsets in the `rowind` and `rowcoef` arrays of the start of the elements for each column. This array contains one entry for each column, plus one more if `collen` is `None`. If `collen` is `None`, the last entry of `start` contains the position in the `rowind` and `rowcoef` arrays at which an extra column would start, if it were present. This value is also the length of the `rowind` and `rowcoef` arrays. May be `None` if the problem contains no coefficients. 
`collen: Iterable[int]` | | Integer array containing the number of nonzero elements in each column. May be `None` if not required. This array is not required if the non-zero coefficients in the `rowind` and `rowcoef` arrays are contiguous, and the `start` array has an additional entry as described above. 
`rowind: Iterable[constraint]` | | Integer array containing the row indices for the nonzero elements in each column. May be `None` if the problem contains no coefficients. If the indices are input contiguously, with the columns in ascending order, the length of the `rowind` array is found by adding the `start` entry for the last column to the `collen` entry for the last column, or if `collen` is `None`, by the additional entry at the end of `start`. 
`rowcoef: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the nonzero element values; length as for `rowind`. May be `None` if the problem contains no coefficients. 
`lb: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the lower bounds on the columns. Use `-xpress.infinity` to represent a lower bound of minus infinity. If this is `None` then all lower bounds are 0 \(zero\). 
`ub: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the upper bounds on the columns. Use `xpress.infinity` to represent an upper bound of plus infinity. If this is `None` then all upper bounds are infinite. 
`objqcol1: Iterable[var]` | | Integer array containing the column index of the first variable in each quadratic term. May be `None` if all objective coefficients are zero. 
`objqcol2: Iterable[var]` | | Integer array containing the column index of the second variable in each quadratic term. May be `None` if all objective coefficients are zero. 
`objqcoef: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the quadratic coefficients. May be `None` if all objective coefficients are zero. 
`qrowind: Iterable[constraint]` | | Integer array containing the indices of rows with quadratic matrices in them. Note that the rows are expected to be defined in `rowtype` as type `L`. May be `None` if the problem contains no quadratic constraints. 
`nrowqcoefs: Iterable[int]` | | Integer array containing the number of nonzeros in each quadratic constraint matrix. May be `None` if the problem contains no quadratic constraints. 
`rowqcol1: Iterable[var]` | | Integer array of size `nqcelem`, where `nqcelem` equals the sum of the elements in `nrowqcoefs` \(i.e. the total number of quadratic matrix elements in all the constraints\). It contains the first column indices of the quadratic matrices. Indices for the first matrix are listed from `0` to `nrowqcoefs[0]-1`, for the second matrix from `nrowqcoefs[0]` to `nrowqcoefs[0]+ nrowqcoefs[1]-1`, etc. May be `None` if the problem contains no quadratic constraints. 
`rowqcol2: Iterable[var]` | | Integer array of size `nqcelem`, containing the second index for the quadratic constraint matrices. May be `None` if the problem contains no quadratic constraints. 
`rowqcoef: Iterable[float]` | | Integer array of size `nqcelem`, containing the coefficients for the quadratic constraint matrices. May be `None` if the problem contains no quadratic constraints.

_**Further information:**_
1. The objective function is of the form `c<sup>T</sup> x+ 0.5 x<sup>T</sup> Qx`. Note that only the upper or lower triangular part of the `Q` matrix is specified, both for the objective and constraints.
2. The double constants `xpress.infinity` and `-xpress.infinity` are defined in the Optimizer library header file.

#### problem.addObj

_**Purpose:**_

   Appends an objective function with the given coefficients to a multi-objective problem. The weight and priority of the objective are set to the given values.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Creation, Multiobjective, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.addObj(colind, objcoef, priority=0, weight=1)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`colind: Iterable[var]` | Integer array containing the indices of the columns whose objective coefficients will change. An index of `-1` indicates that the fixed part of the objective function on the right hand side should change. 
`objcoef: Iterable[float]` | Double array giving the new objective function coefficients. 
`priority: int` | An integer defining the relative priority for the new objective \(only relevant for multi-objective problems\). Higher values mean higher priority. During optimization, objectives with the same priority are combined together in a weighted sum. 
`weight: float` | A double defining the weight for the new objective \(only relevant for multi-objective problems\). If the weight is negative, the sense of this objective is reversed. 

_**Further information:**_
1. This function cannot be called while the current problem is being solved or when it is in an interrupted state. Use `problem.postSolve` to restore the problem to a non-solving state.
2. If all objectives have equal priority but different weights, a blended \(weighted-sum\) approach is applied. For cases where each objective has a different priority but the same weight, a lexicographic approach is applied. The highest priority objective is optimized first. In the second and subsequent iterations, all objectives from previous iterations are fixed to their optimal values within tolerances. If both different priorities and different weights are passed, a hybrid approach is applied: Xpress will solve the problem once for each distinct objective priority that is defined, optimizing in each iteration a linear combination of the objective functions with the same priority.
3. The optimization sense of the first objective defines the default sense for all objectives. To revert the sense of an objective in relation to the first objective, assign it a negative `weight`. For example, if the first objective is set to be maximized, further objectives to be minimized can be declared with `weight=-1`.
4. Argument ``colind`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.chgObjN`, `problem.getObjN`, `problem.delObj`, `problem.chgObj`.

#### problem.chgObjN

_**Purpose:**_

   Modifies one or more coefficients of an objective function in a multi-objective problem. If the objective already exists, any coefficients not present in the `colind`and `objcoef`arrays will unchanged. If the objective does not exist, it will be added to the problem.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Modification, Multiobjective, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.chgObjN(objidx, colind, objcoef)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`objidx: int` | Index of the objective function to add or modify. 
`colind: Iterable[var]` | Integer array containing the indices of the columns whose objective coefficients will change. An index of `-1` indicates that the fixed part of the objective function on the right hand side should change. 
`objcoef: Iterable[float]` | Double array giving the new objective function coefficients. 

_**Further information:**_
1. When `objidx=0`, this function is equivalent to `problem.chgObj`.
2. Any objectives with `idx < objidx` that do not already exist will be added to the problem with all zero coefficients.
3. This function cannot be called while the current problem is being solved or when it is in an interrupted state. Use `problem.postSolve` to restore the problem to a non-solving state.
4. Argument ``colind`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.addObj`, `problem.getObjN`, `problem.delObj`, `problem.chgObj`.

#### problem.delObj

_**Purpose:**_

   Removes an objective function from the problem. Any objectives with `index > objidx`will be shifted down.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Creation, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.delObj(objidx)`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`objidx: int` | Index of the objective to remove. 

_**Further information:**_
1. If the problem has only one objective, `problem.delObj` clears the objective, but `OBJECTIVES` remains set to `1`.
2. This function cannot be called while the current problem is being solved or when it is in an interrupted state. Use `problem.postSolve` to restore the problem to a non-solving state.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.chgObjN`, `problem.addObj`, `problem.getObjN`.

#### problem.interrupt

_**Purpose:**_

   Interrupts the Optimizer algorithms.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Solution Process, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.interrupt(reason=xpress.enums.StopType.USER)`

_**Argument:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`reason: StopType` |  | The reason for stopping. Possible reasons are:
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.NONE` | do not stop;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.TIMELIMIT` | time limit hit;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.WORKLIMIT` | work limit hit;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.CTRLC` | control C hit;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.NODELIMIT` | node limit hit;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.ITERLIMIT` | iteration limit hit;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.MIPGAP` | MIP gap is sufficiently small;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.SOLLIMIT` | solution limit hit;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.USER` | user interrupt;
&nbsp; | `xpress.StopType.NEXTOBJECTIVE` | stop the current solve, but continue with solving the next objective \(see below\);
&nbsp; | `>= 1000` | user defined value.

_**Further information:**_
1. The `problem.interrupt` command can be called from any callback.
2. The range of values below 1000 is reserved for future extension. The behavior of the function is undefined if `reason` is smaller than 1000 and not one of the values listed above.
3. When solving a multi-objective problem, calling `problem.interrupt` with `NEXTOBJECTIVE` instructs the Optimizer to accept the current solution and proceed with solving the next objective. For example, this can be used in the `checktime` callback to implement a different time limit for each objective. If no solution has been found, no objective fixing will take place. The `SOLVESTATUS` attribute reflects the status of the final solve: in particular, if the final objective was solved to optimality then `SOLVESTATUS` will be `COMPLETED`, even if earlier objectives were interrupted. If a single-objective solve, or the final solve of a multi-objective problem, is interrupted with status `NEXTOBJECTIVE`, then `SOLVESTATUS` will be `INTERRUPTED` and `STOPSTATUS` will be `NEXTOBJECTIVE`.

_**Related topics:**_
None.

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`objqcoef: float` | The objective function coefficient. 

_**Further information:**_
1. `objqcoef` is the coefficient in the quadratic Hessian matrix. For example, if the objective function has the term \[3x<sub>1</sub> x<sub>2</sub> + 3x<sub>2</sub> x<sub>1</sub> \]/2 the value retrieved by `problem.getQObj` is `3.0` and if the objective function has the term \[6x<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> \]/2 the value retrieved by `problem.getQObj` is `6.0`.
2. Arguments ``objqcol1`,  `objqcol2`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getMQObj`, `problem.chgQObj`, `problem.chgMQObj`.

#### problem.getDirs

_**Purpose:**_

   Used to return the directives that have been loaded into a matrix. Priorities, forced branching directions and pseudo costs can be returned. If called after presolve, `problem.getDirs`will get the directives for the presolved problem.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Information, Branching, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `indices, prios, branchdirs, uppseudo, downpseudo = problem.getDirs()`

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`indices: list[int]` | Integer array containing the column numbers \( `0`, `1`, `2`,...\) or negative values corresponding to special ordered sets \(the first set numbered `-1`, the second numbered `-2`,...\). 
`prios: list[int]` | Integer array containing the priorities for the columns and sets, where columns/sets with smallest priority will be branched on first. 
`branchdirs: list[str]` | Character array containing the branching direction for each column or set:
&nbsp; | `U` | the entity is to be forced up;
&nbsp; | `D` | the entity is to be forced down;
&nbsp; | `N` | not specified.
 | 
`uppseudo: list[float]` | Double array containing the up pseudo costs for the columns and sets. 
`downpseudo: list[float]` | Double array containing the down pseudo costs for the columns and sets. 

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.loadDirs`, `problem.loadPresolveDirs`.

#### problem.getPresolveMap

_**Purpose:**_

   Returns the mapping of the row and column numbers from the presolve problem back to the original problem.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Information, Presolve, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `rowmap, colmap = problem.getPresolveMap()`

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`rowmap: list[int]` | Integer array of length `ROWS` containing the row maps. 
`colmap: list[int]` | Integer array of length `COLS` containing the column maps. 

_**Further information:**_
1. This function applies to linear and convex quadratic \(including second order conic\) problems only.
2. The presolved problem can contain rows or columns that do not map to anything in the original problem. An example of this are cuts created during the MIP solve and temporarily added to the presolved problem. It is also possible that the presolver will introduce new rows or columns. For any row or column that does not have a mapping to a row or column in the original problem, the corresponding entry in the returned `rowmap` and `colmap` arrays will be `-1`.

_**Related topics:**_
 the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.getRHSRange

#### problem.getMIPEntities

_**Purpose:**_

   Retrieves integr and entity information about a problem. It must be called before`problem.mipOptimize`if the presolve option is used.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Information, MIP Entities, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `coltype, colind, limit, settype, start, setcols, refval = problem.getMIPEntities()`

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`coltype: list[str]` | Character array of length `MIPENTS`containing the entity types. The types will be one of:
&nbsp; | `B` | binary variables;
&nbsp; | `I` | integer variables;
&nbsp; | `P` | partial integer variables;
&nbsp; | `S` | semi-continuous variables;
&nbsp; | `R` | semi-continuous integer variables.
 | 
`colind: list[int]` | Integer array of length `MIPENTS` containing the column indices of the MIP entities. 
`limit: list[float]` | Double array of length `MIPENTS` containing the limits for the partial integer variables and lower bounds for the semi-continuous and semi-continuous integer variables \(any entries in the positions corresponding to binary and integer variables will be meaningless\). 
`settype: list[str]` | Character array of length `SETS`containing the set types. The set types will be one of:
&nbsp; | `1` | SOS1 type sets;
&nbsp; | `2` | SOS2 type sets.
 | 
`start: list[int]` | Integer array containing the offsets into the `setcols` and `refval` arrays indicating the start of each set. This array must be of length `SETS+1`, the last element will contain the offset where set `SETS+1` would start, and equals the length of the `setcols` and `refval` arrays, `SETMEMBERS`. 
`setcols: list[int]` | Integer array of length `SETMEMBERS` containing the columns in each set. 
`refval: list[float]` | Double array of length `SETMEMBERS` containing the reference row entries for each member of the sets. These define the order for SOS2 constraints and may be used in branching for both types. 

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.loadMIP`, `problem.loadMIQP`.

#### problem.getRowFlags

_**Purpose:**_

   Retrieve if a range of rows have been set up as special rows.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Information, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `flags = problem.getRowFlags(first=0, last=ROWS-1)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`first: int` | First row index to be checked 
`last: int` | Last row index to be checked 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`flags: list[int]` | Integer array of length `last-first+1` containing type of information \(see below\) 

_**Further information:**_
1. The `flags` array returns a bitvector for each row defining all the information that is currently attached to that row:
 * `xpress.RowFlag.QUADRATIC`: The row has quadratic coefficients.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.DELAYED`: The row is marked as a delayed row.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.MODELCUT`: The row is marked as a model cut.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.INDICATOR`: The row is used as an indicator.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.NONLINEAR`: The row has nonlinear coefficients.
2. Arguments ``first`,  `last`` may contain either`xpress.constraint` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.clearRowFlags`

#### problem.clearRowFlags

_**Purpose:**_

   Clears extra information attached to a range of rows.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Modification, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.clearRowFlags(flags, first=0, last=ROWS-1)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`flags: Iterable[int]` | Integer array of length `last-first+1` including type of extra information to remove \(see below\) 
`first: int` | First row index to be checked 
`last: int` | Last row index to be checked 

_**Further information:**_
1. The `flags` array consists of a bitvector for each row defining types of information to remove:
 * `xpress.RowFlag.QUADRATIC`: Remove all quadratic coefficients.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.DELAYED`: The row will not be a delayed row.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.MODELCUT`: The row will not be a model cut.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.INDICATOR`: Remove indicators associated to the row.
 * `xpress.RowFlag.NONLINEAR`: Remove any nonlinear coefficients.
2. Arguments ``first`,  `last`` may contain either`xpress.constraint` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getRowFlags`

#### problem.getMQObj

_**Purpose:**_

   Returns the nonzeros in the quadratic objective coefficients matrix for the columns in a given range. To achieve maximum efficiency, `problem.getMQObj`returns the lower triangular part of this matrix only.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Problem Information, Quadratic, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `start, colind, objqcoef = problem.getMQObj(first=0, last=COLS-1)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`first: int` | First column in the range. 
`last: int` | Last column in the range. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`start: list[int]` | Integer array of length `last-first+2` containing indices indicating the starting offsets in the `colind` and `objqcoef` arrays for each requested column. Column `i` starts at position `start[i]` in the `colind` and `objqcoef` arrays, and has `start[i+1]-start[i]` elements in it. 
`colind: list[int]` | Integer array containing the column indices of the nonzero elements in the lower triangular part of `Q`. 
`objqcoef: list[float]` | Double array containing the nonzero element values. 

_**Further information:**_
1. The objective function is of the form `c<sup>T</sup> x+0.5x<sup>T</sup> Qx`. Note that only the upper or lower triangular part of the `Q` matrix is returned.
2. Arguments ``first`,  `last`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.chgMQObj`, `problem.chgQObj`, `problem.getQObj`.

#### problem.writeBasis

_**Purpose:**_

   Writes the current basis to a file for later input into the Optimizer.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
File IO, LP, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.writeBasis(filename="", flags="")`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`filename: str` | | A string of up to `MAXPROBNAMELENGTH` characters containing the file name from which the basis is to be written. If omitted, the default _problem_name_ is used with a `.bss` extension. 
`flags: str` |  | Flags to pass to `problem.writeBasis`:
&nbsp; | `i` | output the internal presolved basis;
&nbsp; | `t` | output a compact advanced form of the basis;
&nbsp; | `n` | output basis file containing current solution values;
&nbsp; | `h` | output values in single precision;
&nbsp; | `p` | output values in full precision \(obsolete as this is now default behavior\);
&nbsp; | `v` | use the provided filename verbatim, without appending the `.bss` extension;
&nbsp; | `z` | compress the output file.

_**Further information:**_
1. The `t` flag is only useful for later input to a similar problem using the `t` flag with `problem.readBasis`.
2. If the Newton barrier or hybrid gradient algorithms have been used for optimization then crossover must have been performed before there is a valid basis. This basis can then be used for restarting the simplex \(primal or dual\) or the hybrid gradient algorithms.
3. `problem.writeBasis` will output the basis for the original problem even if the matrix has been presolved.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getBasis`, `problem.readBasis`.

#### problem.writeSol

_**Purpose:**_

   Writes the current solution to a CSV format ASCII file, _problem_name_ `.asc`\(and `.hdr`\).

_**Topic areas:**_ 
File IO, Solution, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.writeSol(filename="", flags="")`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`filename: str` | | A string of up to `MAXPROBNAMELENGTH` characters containing the file name to which the solution is to be written. If omitted, the default _problem_name_ will be used. The extensions `.hdr` and `.asc` will be appended. 
`flags: str` |  | Flags to control which optional fields are output:
&nbsp; | `s` | sequence number;
&nbsp; | `n` | name;
&nbsp; | `t` | type;
&nbsp; | `b` | basis status;
&nbsp; | `a` | activity;
&nbsp; | `c` | cost \(columns\), slack \(rows\);
&nbsp; | `l` | lower bound;
&nbsp; | `u` | upper bound;
&nbsp; | `d` | dj \(column; reduced costs\), dual value \(rows; shadow prices\);
&nbsp; | `r` | right hand side \(rows\).
&nbsp; |  | If no flags are specified, all fields are output.
&nbsp; | Additional flags:
&nbsp; | `p` | outputs in full precision;
&nbsp; | `q` | only outputs vectors with nonzero optimum value;
&nbsp; | `x` | output the current LP solution instead of the MIP solution;
&nbsp; | `z` | compress the output file.

_**Related controls:**_

_Double_
  
_Name_ | _Description_
---------- | ----------
`OUTPUTTOL` | Tolerance on print values.

_String_
  
_Name_ | _Description_
---------- | ----------
`OUTPUTMASK` | Mask to restrict the row and column names output to file.

_**Further information:**_
1. This function currently does not apply to general nonlinear problems.
2. The command produces two readable files: `filename.hdr` \(the solution header file\) and `filename.asc` \(the CSV format solution file\). The header file contains summary information, all in one line. The ASCII file contains one line of information for each row and column in the problem. Any fields appearing in the `.asc` file will be in the order the flags are described above. The order that the flags are specified by the user is irrelevant.
3. Additionally, the mask control `OUTPUTMASK` may be used to control which names are reported to the ASCII file. Only vectors whose names match `OUTPUTMASK` are output. `OUTPUTMASK` is set by default to " `????????` ", so that all vectors are output.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getSolution`, `problem.writePrtSol`.

This function currently does not apply to general nonlinear problems.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getSolution`, `problem.readBinSol`, `problem.writeSol`, `problem.writePrtSol`.

#### problem.writePrtSol

_**Purpose:**_

   Writes the current solution to a fixed format ASCII file, _problem_name_ `.prt`.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
File IO, Solution, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.writePrtSol(filename="", flags="")`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`filename: str` | | A string of up to `MAXPROBNAMELENGTH` characters containing the file name to which the solution is to be written. If omitted, the default _problem_name_ will be used. The extension `.prt` will be appended. 
`flags: str` |  | Flags for `problem.writePrtSol`are:
&nbsp; | `x` | write the LP solution instead of the current MIP solution;
&nbsp; | `v` | use the provided filename verbatim, without appending the `.prt` extension;
&nbsp; | `z` | write a compressed output file;
&nbsp; | `s` | include classical sensitivity analysis.

_**Related controls:**_

_Integer_
  
_Name_ | _Description_
---------- | ----------
`MAXPAGELINES` | Number of lines between page breaks.

_Double_
  
_Name_ | _Description_
---------- | ----------
`OUTPUTTOL` | Tolerance on print values.

_**Further information:**_
1. This function currently does not apply to general nonlinear problems.
2. The fixed width ASCII format created by this command is not as readily useful as that produced by `problem.writeSol`. The main purpose of `problem.writePrtSol` is to create a file that can be sent directly to a printer. The format of this fixed format ASCII file is described in Appendix the Optimizer Reference Manual.
3. To create a prt file for a previously saved solution, the solution must first be loaded with the `problem.readBinSol` function.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getSolution`, `problem.readBinSol` `problem.writeBinSol`, `problem.writeSol`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.writeSlxSol

_**Purpose:**_

   Creates an ASCII solution file \( `.slx`\) using a similar format to MPS files. These files can be read back into the Optimizer using the`problem.readSlxSol`function.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
File IO, Solution, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.writeSlxSol(filename="", flags="")`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`filename: str` | | A string of up to `MAXPROBNAMELENGTH` characters containing the file name to which the solution is to be written. If omitted, the default _problem_name_ is used with a `.slx` extension. 
`flags: str` |  | Flags to pass to `problem.writeSlxSol`:

&nbsp; | `p` | use full precision for numerical values \(obsolete as this is now default behavior\);
&nbsp; | `s` | including slack variables;
&nbsp; | `d` | LP solution only: including dual variables;
&nbsp; | `r` | LP solution only: including reduced cost;

&nbsp; | `z` | compress the output file.

_**Related topics:**_

#### problem.getPrimalRay

_**Purpose:**_

   Retrieves a primal ray \(primal unbounded direction\) for the current problem, if the problem is found to be unbounded.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Solution, LP, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `ray = problem.getPrimalRay()`

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`ray: Optional[list[float]]` | Double array of length `COLS` containing the ray, or `None` if the Optimizer is not able to return a primal ray. 

_**Further information:**_
1. This function applies to linear and convex quadratic \(including second order conic\) problems only.
2. It is possible to retrieve a primal ray only when, after solving an LP problem, the final status \( `LPSTATUS`\) is xpress.LPStatus.UNBOUNDED.
3. Primal rays are not post-solved. If the problem is in a presolved state, the primal ray that is returned will be for the presolved problem. If the problem was solved with presolve on and has been restored to the original state \(the default behavior\), this function will not be able to return a ray. To ensure that a primal ray can be obtained, it is recommended to solve a problem with presolve turned off \( `PRESOLVE` = 0\).

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getDualRay`.

#### problem.getDualRay

_**Purpose:**_

   Retrieves a dual ray \(dual unbounded direction\) for the current problem, if the problem is found to be infeasible.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Solution, LP, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `ray = problem.getDualRay()`

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`ray: Optional[list[float]]` | Double array of length `ROWS` containing the ray, or `None` if the Optimizer is not able to return a dual ray. 

_**Further information:**_
1. It is possible to retrieve a dual ray only when, after solving an LP problem, the final status \( `LPSTATUS`\) is `xpress.LPStatus.INFEAS`.
2. Dual rays are not post-solved. If the problem is in a presolved state, the dual ray that is returned will be for the presolved problem. If the problem was solved with presolve on and has been restored to the original state \(the default behavior\), this function will not be able to return a ray. To ensure that a dual ray can be obtained, it is recommended to solve a problem with presolve turned off \( `PRESOLVE` = 0\).

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getPrimalRay`.

#### problem.loadMipSol

_**Purpose:**_

   Loads a starting MIP solution for the problem into the Optimizer.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Solution, MIP Entities, Data Input, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `status = problem.loadMipSol(x)`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description
---------- | ---------- 
`x: Iterable[float]` | Double array of length `COLS` \(for the original problem and not the presolve problem\) containing the values of the variables. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`status: int` | The status. The status is one of:
&nbsp; | `-1` | Solution rejected because an error occurred;
&nbsp; | `0` | Solution accepted.

_**Further information:**_
1. When a solution is loaded, the solution is placed in temporary storage until the MIP solve is started. Only after the MIP solve has commenced and any presolve has been applied, will the loaded solution be checked and possibly accepted as a new incumbent integer solution. There are no checks performed on the solution before the MIP solve and the returned status in `problem.loadMipSol` will always be `0` for accepted.
2. Loaded solution values will automatically be adjusted to fit within the current problem bounds.
3. It is recommended to use `problem.addMipSol` instead of `problem.loadMipSol`. `problem.addMipSol` can be called both before a solve, to load a starting solution, and during a MIP solve, to load new solutions within callbacks. `problem.addMipSol` also allows for loading of infeasible or partial solutions and comes with a callback to check the status of loaded solutions.
4. This function cannot be called while the current problem is being solved or when it is in an interrupted state. Use `problem.postSolve` to restore the problem to a non-solving state.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.addMipSol`, `problem.getSolution`.

#### problem.getBasis

_**Purpose:**_

   Returns the current basis into the user's data arrays.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Linear Algebra, LP, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `rowstat, colstat = problem.getBasis()`

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`rowstat: list[int]` | Integer array of length`ORIGINALROWS`containing the basis status of the slack, surplus or artificial variable associated with each row. The status will be one of:
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.NONBASIC_LOWER (0)` | slack, surplus or artificial is non-basic at lower bound;
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.BASIC (1)` | slack, surplus or artificial is basic;
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.NONBASIC_UPPER (2)` | slack or surplus is non-basic at upper bound.
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.SUPERBASIC (3)` | slack or surplus is super-basic.
 | 
`colstat: list[int]` | Integer array of length`ORIGINALCOLS`containing the basis status of the columns in the constraint matrix. The status will be one of:
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.NONBASIC_LOWER (0)` | variable is non-basic at lower bound, or superbasic at zero if the variable has no lower bound;
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.BASIC (1)` | variable is basic;
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.NONBASIC_UPPER (2)` | variable is non-basic at upper bound;
&nbsp; | `xpress.BasisStatus.SUPERBASIC (3)` | variable is super-basic.
 | 

_**Further information:**_
The basis information is always for the original \(unpresolved\) model.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getPresolveBasis`, `problem.loadBasis`, `problem.loadPresolveBasis`.

#### problem.addManagedCuts

_**Purpose:**_

   Adds cuts to the Optimizer's internal cut pool from within the _cutround_callback set by`problem.addCutRoundCallback`. The cuts will be added to an internal pool of cuts managed by the Optimizer. The Optimizer will use internal priorities to dynamically load violated cuts from this pool into branch-and-bound node problems and remove inactive cuts. Cuts can be either _local_or _global_. Cuts flagged as _local_are assumed to be valid only for the the current node of the branch-and-bound search or any of its descendants. Global cuts are assumed to be valid for the whole problem and might be used on any node of the branch-and-bound search tree. The cuts should be formulated in the original space of variables and will automatically be presolved.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Callback, Cuts, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.addManagedCuts(globalvalid, rowtype, rhs, start, colind, cutcoef)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`globalvalid: int` | | Nonzero if the cuts should be assumed to be valid for the whole problem. If zero, cuts will be assumed to be valid only for the current node and its descendants. 
`rowtype: Iterable[str]` |  | Character array containing the row types:
&nbsp; | `L` | indicates a≤ row;
&nbsp; | `G` | indicates a≥ row;
&nbsp; | `E` | indicates an = row.
`rhs: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the right hand side elements for the cuts. 
`start: Iterable[int]` | | Integer array containing offset into the `colind` and `cutcoef` arrays indicating the start of each cut. This array has one entry for each cut, plus one more entry indicating where an additional cut would start, if it were present. 
`colind: Iterable[var]` | | Integer array containing the column indices in the cuts. 
`cutcoef: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the matrix values for the cuts. 

_**Further information:**_
1. This function applies to linear and convex quadratic \(including second order conic\) problems only.
2. The columns and elements of the cuts must be stored contiguously in the `colind` and `cutcoef` arrays passed to `problem.addManagedCuts`. The starting point of each cut must be stored in the `start` array. To determine the length of the final cut, the `start` array must have one more element than the number of cuts, with the last element containing the position in `colind` and `cutcoef` where an extra cut would start, if it were present. This last entry denotes the number of nonzeros in the added cuts.
3. Cuts will not be loaded into the problem if `CUTSTRATEGY` is set to zero.
4. Cuts added by `problem.addManagedCuts` cannot be retrieved by `problem.getCutList` or `problem.getCPCutList`.
5. This function can only be called from a callback function set by `problem.addCutRoundCallback`.
6. Argument ``colind`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.addCutRoundCallback`, `problem.addCuts`, `CUTSTRATEGY`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.addCuts

_**Purpose:**_

   Adds cuts directly to the matrix at the current node. The cuts will automatically be added to the cut pool. Cuts added to a node will automatically be inherited on any descendant node, unless explicitly deleted with a call to`problem.delCuts`.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Cuts, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.addCuts(cuttype, rowtype, rhs, start, colind, cutcoef)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`cuttype: Iterable[int]` | | Integer array containing the user assigned cut types. The cut types can be any integer chosen by the user, and are used to identify the cuts in other cut manager routines using user supplied parameters. The cut type can be interpreted as an integer or a bitmap - see `problem.delCuts`. 
`rowtype: Iterable[str]` |  | Character array containing the row types:
&nbsp; | `L` | indicates a≤ row;
&nbsp; | `G` | indicates a≥ row;
&nbsp; | `E` | indicates an = row.
`rhs: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the right hand side elements for the cuts. 
`start: Iterable[int]` | | Integer array containing offset into the `colind` and `cutcoef` arrays indicating the start of each cut. This array has one entry for each cut, plus one more entry indicating where an additional cut would start, if it were present. 
`colind: Iterable[var]` | | Integer array containing the column indices in the cuts. 
`cutcoef: Iterable[float]` | | Double array containing the matrix values for the cuts. 

_**Further information:**_
1. The columns and elements of the cuts must be stored contiguously in the `colind` and `cutcoef` arrays passed to `problem.addCuts`. The starting point of each cut must be stored in the `start` array. To determine the length of the final cut, the `start` array must have one more element than the number of cuts, with the last element containing the position in `colind` and `cutcoef` where an extra cut would start, if it were present. This last entry denotes the number of nonzeros in the added cuts.
2. The cuts added to the matrix are always added at the end of the matrix and the number of rows is always set to the original number rows plust the number of cuts added. If `n` cuts have been added, then the rows `0`,..., `ROWS` - `n` - `1` are the original rows, whilst the rows `ROWS` - `n`,..., `ROWS` - `1` are the added cuts. The number of cuts can be found by consulting the `CUTS` problem attribute.
3. This function should be called only from within callback functions set by either `problem.addNodeLPSolvedCallback`, `problem.addOptnodeCallback`, `problem.addPreIntsolCallback` or `problem.addPrenodeCallback`.
4. Argument ``colind`` may contain either`xpress.var` objects or integer indices.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.addRows`, `problem.delCPCuts`, `problem.delCuts`, `problem.getCPCutList`, `problem.getCutList`, `problem.loadCuts`, `problem.storeCuts`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.delCuts

_**Purpose:**_

   Deletes cuts from the matrix at the current node. Cuts from the parent node which have been automatically restored may be deleted as well as cuts added to the current node using`problem.addCuts`or`problem.loadCuts`. The cuts to be deleted can be specified in a number of ways. If a cut is ruled out by any one of the criteria it will not be deleted.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Cuts, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.delCuts(basis, cuttype=0, interp=-1, delta=-xpress.infinity, cutind=None)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`basis: int` | | Ensures the basis will be valid if set to `1`. If set to `0`, cuts with non-basic slacks may be deleted. 
`cuttype: int` | | User defined type of the cut to be deleted. 
`interp: int` |  | Way in which the cut `cuttype`is interpreted:
&nbsp; | `-1` | match all cut types;
&nbsp; | `1` | treat cut types as numbers;
&nbsp; | `2` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - delete if any bit matches any bit set in `cuttype`;
&nbsp; | `3` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - delete if all bits match those set in `cuttype`.
`delta: float` | | Only delete cuts with an absolute slack value greater than `delta`. To delete all the cuts, this argument should be set to `-xpress.infinity`. 
`cutind: Iterable[poolcut]` | | Array containing the cuts which are to be deleted. This array may be `None` to delete all cuts. 

_**Further information:**_
1. It is usually best to drop only those cuts with basic slacks, otherwise the basis will no longer be valid and it may take many iterations to recover an optimal basis. If the `basis` parameter is set to `1`, this will ensure that cuts with non-basic slacks will not be deleted even if the other parameters specify that these cuts should be deleted. It is highly recommended that the `basis` parameter is always set to `1`.
2. The cuts to be deleted can also be specified by the size of the slack variable for the cut. Only those cuts with a slack value greater than the `delta` parameter will be deleted.
3. A list of indices of the cuts to be deleted can also be provided. The list of active cuts at a node can be obtained with the `problem.getCutList` command.
4. This function should be called only from within callback functions set by either `problem.addOptnodeCallback`, `problem.addPrenodeCallback`, `problem.addPreIntsolCallback` or `problem.addNodeLPSolvedCallback`.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.addCuts`, `problem.delCPCuts`, `problem.getCutList`, `problem.loadCuts`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.delCPCuts

_**Purpose:**_

   During the branch and bound search, cuts are stored in the cut pool to be applied at descendant nodes. These cuts may be removed from a given node using`problem.delCuts`, but if this is to be applied in a large number of cases, it may be preferable to remove the cut completely from the cut pool. This is achieved using `problem.delCPCuts`.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Cuts, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `problem.delCPCuts(cuttype=0, interp=-1, cutind=None)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`cuttype: int` | | User defined cut type to match against. 
`interp: int` |  | Way in which the cut `cuttype`is interpreted:
&nbsp; | `-1` | match all cut types;
&nbsp; | `1` | treat cut types as numbers;
&nbsp; | `2` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - delete if any bit matches any bit set in `cuttype`;
&nbsp; | `3` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - delete if all bits match those set in `cuttype`.
`cutind: Iterable[poolcut]` | | Array containing the cuts which are to be deleted. This array may be `None` to delete all cuts. 

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.addCuts`, `problem.delCuts`, `problem.loadCuts`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.getCutList

_**Purpose:**_

   Retrieves a list of cut objects for the cuts active at the current node.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Cuts, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `cutind = problem.getCutList(cuttype=0, interp=-1)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`cuttype: int` | | User defined type of the cuts to be returned. A value of `-1` indicates return all active cuts. 
`interp: int` |  | Way in which the cut type is interpreted:
&nbsp; | `-1` | get all cuts;
&nbsp; | `1` | treat cut types as numbers;
&nbsp; | `2` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - get cut if any bit matches any bit set in `cuttype`;
&nbsp; | `3` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - get cut if all bits match those set in `cuttype`.

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`cutind: list[poolcut]` | Array containing the cut objects. 

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.getCPCutList`, `problem.getCPCuts`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.getCPCutList

_**Purpose:**_

   Returns a list of cut indices from the cut pool.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Cuts, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `cutind, viol = problem.getCPCutList(cuttype=0, interp=-1, delta=-xpress.infinity)`

_**Arguments:**_

Name | Value |  Description
---------- | ---------- | ----------
`cuttype: int` | | The user defined type of the cuts to be returned. 
`interp: int` |  | Way in which the cut type is interpreted:
&nbsp; | `-1` | get all cuts;
&nbsp; | `1` | treat cut types as numbers;
&nbsp; | `2` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - get cut if any bit matches any bit set in `cuttype`;
&nbsp; | `3` | treat cut types as bit-vectors \(compare the Optimizer Reference Manual\) - get cut if all bits match those set in `cuttype`.
`delta: float` | | Only those cuts with a signed violation greater than delta will be returned. 

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description
---------- | ---------- 
`cutind: list[poolcut]` | Array containing the cut objects. 
`viol: list[float]` | Double array containing the values of the signed violations of the cuts. 

_**Further information:**_
1. The violated cuts can be obtained by setting the `delta` parameter to the size of the \(signed\) violation required. If unviolated cuts are required as well, `delta` may be set to `-xpress.infinity` which is defined in the library header file.
2. In case of a cut of type ' `L` ', the violation equals the negative of the slack associated with the row of the cut. In case of a cut of type ' `G` ', the violation equals the slack associated with the row of the cut. For cuts of type ' `E` ', the violation equals the absolute value of the slack.
3. Please note that the violations returned are absolute violations, while feasibility is checked by the Optimizer in the scaled problem.

_**Related topics:**_
`problem.delCPCuts`, `problem.getCPCuts`, `problem.getCutList`, `problem.loadCuts`, `problem.getCutMap`, `problem.getCutSlack`, the Optimizer Reference Manual.

#### problem.getCPCuts

_**Purpose:**_

   Returns cuts from the cut pool.

_**Topic areas:**_ 
Cuts, Optimizer

_**Synopsis:**_

   `cuttype, rowtype, start, colind, cutcoef, rhs = problem.getCPCuts(rowind)`

_**Argument:**_

Name |  Description

_**Return value:**_

Value | Description

`cuttype: list[int]` | Integer array containing the cut types. 
`rowtype: list[str]` | Character array containing the sense of the cuts \( `L`, `G`, or `E`\). 
`start: list[int]` | Integer array containing the offsets into the `colind` and `cutcoef` arrays. The last element indicates where an additional cut would start, if it were present. 
`colind: list[int]` | Integer array containing the column indices of the cuts. 
`cutcoef: list[float]` | Double array containing the matrix values. 
`rhs: list[float]` | Double array containing the right hand side elements for the cuts.
